title: LDAP: the server could not bind to the directory
plain_english: Before it can look anyone up, FreeRADIUS binds to LDAP with the module's own identity (or, in bind-as-user mode, with the user's). That bind failed, so every user fails regardless of their password. One exception: if the DN that failed to bind is the user's own DN, this is really a wrong user password.

causes.cause: The identity or password in mods-available/ldap is wrong, expired, or locked.
causes.next_check: From the RADIUS host: ldapsearch -x -H <server> -D '<identity>' -w '<password>' -b '<base_dn>' '(objectClass=*)' -s base; fix the credentials the directory rejects.

causes.cause: The directory is unreachable or the TLS setup is wrong ('Hit reconnection limit', ldap_initialize failures): wrong host/port, ldaps vs start_tls, or an untrusted server certificate.
causes.next_check: Check server, port, start_tls and the tls { ca_file } section in mods-available/ldap; test the TLS path with openssl s_client -connect <server>:636.

causes.cause: Bind-as-user mode and the user's password is wrong.
causes.next_check: If the failing bind DN is the user's DN (cn=alice,...), treat this as a credential failure and test the user's password with ldapwhoami.
